full_name: Risk Of Bias In Non-randomised Studies - of Interventions
applies_to: Non-randomised studies of the effects of interventions (cohort, case-control, quasi-randomized, etc.)
source: Sterne JAC, Hernan MA, Reeves BC, et al. ROBINS-I: a tool for assessing risk of bias in non-randomised studies of interventions. BMJ 2016;355:i4919. Tool reproduced from riskofbias.info.
assessed_per: result (outcome), for a specified target trial and effect of interest

1.1.text: Is there potential for confounding of the effect of intervention in this study?

1.2.text: If N/PN to 1.1: [proceed to domain judgement, low risk]. Was the analysis based on splitting participants' follow-up time according to intervention received?

1.3.text: If Y/PY to 1.2: Were intervention discontinuations or switches likely to be related to factors that are prognostic for the outcome?

1.4.text: Did the authors use an appropriate analysis method that controlled for all the important confounding domains?

1.5.text: If Y/PY to 1.4: Were confounding domains that were controlled for measured validly and reliably by the variables available in this study?

1.6.text: Did the authors control for any post-intervention variables that could have been affected by the intervention?

1.7.text: If Y/PY to 1.2: Did the authors use an appropriate analysis method that controlled for all the important confounding domains and for time-varying confounding?

1.8.text: If Y/PY to 1.7: Were the confounding domains that were controlled for measured validly and reliably by the variables available in this study?

D2.name: Bias in selection of participants into the study

2.1.text: Was selection of participants into the study (or into the analysis) based on participant characteristics observed after the start of intervention?

2.2.text: If Y/PY to 2.1: Were the post-intervention variables that influenced selection likely to be associated with intervention?

2.3.text: If Y/PY to 2.2: Were the post-intervention variables that influenced selection likely to be influenced by the outcome or a cause of the outcome?

2.4.text: Do start of follow-up and start of intervention coincide for most participants?

2.5.text: If Y/PY to 2.2 and 2.3, or N/PN to 2.4: Were adjustment techniques used that are likely to correct for the presence of selection biases?

3.2.text: Was the information used to define intervention groups recorded at the start of the intervention?

3.3.text: Could classification of intervention status have been affected by knowledge of the outcome or risk of the outcome?

D4.name: Bias due to deviations from intended interventions

4.1.text: Were there deviations from the intended intervention beyond what would be expected in usual practice?

4.2.text: If Y/PY to 4.1: Were these deviations from intended intervention unbalanced between groups and likely to have affected the outcome?

4.3.text: [Effect of adhering] Were important co-interventions balanced across intervention groups?

4.4.text: [Effect of adhering] Was the intervention implemented successfully for most participants?

4.5.text: [Effect of adhering] Did study participants adhere to the assigned intervention regimen?

4.6.text: If N/PN to 4.3, 4.4 or 4.5: Was an appropriate analysis used to estimate the effect of adhering to the intervention?

5.1.text: Were outcome data available for all, or nearly all, participants?

5.2.text: Were participants excluded due to missing data on intervention status?

5.3.text: Were participants excluded due to missing data on other variables needed for the analysis?

5.4.text: If PN/N to 5.1, or Y/PY to 5.2 or 5.3: Are the proportion of participants and reasons for missing data similar across interventions?

5.5.text: If PN/N to 5.1, or Y/PY to 5.2 or 5.3: Is there evidence that results were robust to the presence of missing data?

6.1.text: Could the outcome measure have been influenced by knowledge of the intervention received?

6.2.text: Were outcome assessors aware of the intervention received by study participants?

6.3.text: Were the methods of outcome assessment comparable across intervention groups?

6.4.text: Were any systematic errors in measurement of the outcome related to intervention received?

D7.name: Bias in selection of the reported result

7.1.text: Is the reported effect estimate likely to be selected, on the basis of the results, from multiple outcome measurements within the outcome domain?

7.2.text: Is the reported effect estimate likely to be selected, on the basis of the results, from multiple analyses of the intervention-outcome relationship?

7.3.text: Is the reported effect estimate likely to be selected, on the basis of the results, from different subgroups?

overall_rule.low: Low risk of bias for all domains.
overall_rule.moderate: Low or moderate risk of bias for all domains (at least one moderate; none serious/critical).
overall_rule.serious: Serious risk of bias in at least one domain, but not critical in any domain.
overall_rule.critical: Critical risk of bias in at least one domain.
overall_rule.no information: No clear indication of serious/critical risk of bias, but a lack of information in one or more key domains (a judgement is required).
